Who We Treat

Who We Treat

Patients managing chronic or high-frequency episodic migraine with meaningful functional impairment across occupational, domestic, or social domains

Those with treatment-refractory headache disorders who have not achieved adequate clinical response through conventional first- or second-line therapies

Conditions

Conditions We Treat

Condition

Chronic Migraine

15 or more headache days per month

Chronic migraine means living with 15 or more headache days per month — at least 8 of which have the quality of a true migraine attack. This is not simply "bad headaches." It is a recognized neurological condition that rewires pain pathways over time. Work, sleep, relationships, and daily life are all affected. Many patients who come to us have tried two, three, or four medications without finding lasting relief. That history doesn't disqualify you — it's exactly why a physician who specializes in this condition matters.

Insurance-accepted for this diagnosis

Condition

Episodic Migraine

Fewer than 15 days/month, but still severely disabling

Episodic migraine typically means fewer than 15 headache days per month — but within those attacks, the experience can be completely disabling: one-sided pain, nausea, and an extreme sensitivity to light and sound that can make any room feel impossible to be in. We also evaluate patients whose migraines are increasing in frequency. Early, precise intervention is one of the most effective ways to prevent episodic migraine from becoming chronic.

Preventive treatment often covered by insurance

Condition

Cluster Headache

Among the most painful conditions in medicine

Cluster headaches are one of the most severe pain conditions documented in medicine — frequently described by patients who have also experienced childbirth or kidney stones as distinctly worse than either. They strike on one side of the head, usually around or behind the eye, and may occur multiple times a day in cycles lasting weeks or months. They are often accompanied by eye redness, tearing, and nasal symptoms on the same side. We treat this condition with the urgency and precision it demands.

Specialist evaluation is essential for this diagnosis

Condition

Tension-Type Headache

The most common headache type — still worth treating properly

Tension-type headaches are the most common headache disorder — a steady, pressing pain that wraps around the head, often described as a tight band or a weight pressing down. While generally less intense than migraine, frequent or chronic tension headaches erode quality of life significantly, especially when they occur alongside or overlap with migraine. We evaluate both patterns together, because they often share root causes and respond to the same treatments.

Often coexists with migraine — combined evaluation recommended

Condition

Neuralgia & Facial Pain

Shooting or burning pain along the nerves of the face or head

Neuralgia refers to pain that originates from a specific nerve rather than from muscle tension or vascular changes. In the head and face, this includes trigeminal neuralgia (sharp, electric-shock pain along the face) and occipital neuralgia (shooting pain from the base of the skull up through the scalp). These conditions are frequently misidentified as migraine or sinus headache and undertreated as a result. Precisely placed nerve blocks — a clinical strength of this practice — can provide relief when general pain medications have failed.

Nerve blocks often provide rapid relief in these cases

Condition

Post-Traumatic Headache

Headache that begins after a head injury or concussion

Post-traumatic headache develops in the days or weeks following a head injury, concussion, or whiplash — and can persist for months or years when not properly evaluated and treated. It often mimics migraine or tension headache but may also present as an entirely new pattern. Post-traumatic headache is real, neurological in origin, and one of the most undertreated conditions in headache medicine. We provide thorough evaluation and a personalized treatment plan designed around your specific post-injury presentation.

Often covered by auto or workers' compensation insurance

Our Approach

How We Think About Your Care

01

Adaptive clinical management

Migraine rarely follows a linear course. We approach every patient relationship as an evolving clinical partnership — continuously reassessing treatment efficacy and recalibrating based on real-world response data.

02

Dynamic diagnostic refinement

An initial diagnosis represents a working clinical hypothesis, not a fixed conclusion. As objective and subjective data accumulate across visits, we refine our diagnostic formulation and modify treatment strategy accordingly.

03

Outcome-driven protocol calibration

No patient is maintained on a therapeutic regimen that has failed to yield meaningful clinical response. We track quantifiable outcomes at every interval and recalibrate proactively — not reactively.

04

Stratified therapeutic escalation

Escalation decisions are governed by clinical evidence, validated safety profiles, and longitudinal neurological risk calculus — not by patient preference or prevailing therapeutic trend.

Treatments

Interventional Protocols

01

Botox for Chronic Migraine

FDA-approved OnabotulinumtoxinA therapy delivered across the standardized 31-site head and neck injection paradigm at 12-week intervals. Among the most rigorously validated preventive therapies for chronic migraine, with demonstrated efficacy across multiple randomized controlled trials.

02

Occipital Nerve Blocks

Precision anesthetic nerve blocks targeting the greater and lesser occipital nerves — capable of interrupting an acute migraine cycle and providing sustained relief in cervicogenic, occipital, and cervicotrigeminal headache presentations.

03

Trigger Point Injections

Targeted myofascial injection therapy addressing pericranial and cervical trigger zones implicated in headache amplification and chronification — an evidence-supported adjunct to individualized migraine treatment protocols.

04

Neuromodulation Strategies

FDA-cleared, non-pharmacologic neuromodulatory devices for acute and preventive migraine management — offering an evidence-based therapeutic avenue for patients with pharmacological intolerance, contraindication, or inadequate first-line response.

05

Infusion Therapy

Physician-supervised IV infusion therapy encompassing acute migraine rescue agents, magnesium sulfate, NAD+ neurological support, and individualized adjunctive formulations — indicated for refractory, high-frequency, and perioperative migraine presentations.

Our Process

What to Expect

01

A complete clinical history, unhurried

Your first visit is designed for depth, not efficiency. We review your complete symptom chronology, therapeutic history, current medications, and the functional burden your condition carries — before forming any clinical impression.

02

A precise, structured diagnosis

Applying ICHD-3 diagnostic criteria, we classify your specific headache phenotype, neurological profile, and clinical burden — establishing a precise diagnostic foundation and a defined therapeutic direction.

03

Customized therapeutic architecture

Your treatment plan is constructed from evidence-validated modalities selected specifically for your diagnosis, clinical history, and therapeutic goals — not a templated pathway, but a clinical design built for your case.

04

Structured longitudinal follow-up

We monitor outcomes at defined intervals, reviewing your clinical response and executing the therapeutic adjustments your case requires. Care within our focused clinical programs is structured as an ongoing clinical relationship — not a single encounter.

Interventional Neurology  ·  Protocol Overview

Dosage & Cumulative Treatment Horizon

The following framework maps the clinical arc of a standard OnabotulinumtoxinA + CGRP pathway regimen across a 12-month treatment horizon. Actual protocols are individualized per patient; this visualization represents the evidence-based structural framework. Hover or tap each cycle to expand clinical detail.

Cycle 1  ·  Weeks 1–12

Initiation & Baseline Establishment

OnabotulinumtoxinA 155u  ·  31-site PREEMPT paradigm
CGRP agent initiated (if indicated)  ·  IV rescue if required

The first treatment cycle establishes the pharmacological foundation. OnabotulinumtoxinA is administered across the standardized 31-site craniocervical injection map, targeting the trigeminal and cervical pain pathways. If CGRP pathway therapy is indicated, it is initiated concurrently in this cycle to allow complementary mechanisms to act across the same neural substrate.

Formal ICHD-3 diagnostic classification confirmed prior to Cycle 1 administration
Baseline headache diary established — frequency, duration, functional impact
Peak OnabotulinumtoxinA effect achieved at Weeks 3–4; full cycle benefit assessed at Week 12
CGRP pathway pharmacokinetics: therapeutic concentration reached by Week 4
IV magnesium rescue available for breakthrough episodes throughout Cycle 1
Cycle 2  ·  Weeks 12–24

Clinical Response Calibration

OnabotulinumtoxinA 155–195u  ·  Protocol adjusted per response
CGRP agent continued or adjusted  ·  Dosage recalibrated

The second cycle is the most clinically instructive. Response data from Cycle 1 — headache frequency delta, functional improvement, tolerability — informs every therapeutic adjustment in this cycle. Dosage may be calibrated between 155 and 195 units based on the physician’s assessment of response pattern and muscle activity in undertreated zones.

Formal Cycle 1 outcomes review at Week 12 against documented baseline
Injection site map reviewed for pattern adjustments — undertreated zones identified and corrected
CGRP agent compliance and tolerability assessed; agent or dosing adjusted if indicated
Most patients report statistically meaningful improvement by Cycle 2 completion
Decision point: continuation, protocol modification, or adjunctive therapy addition
12-Month Horizon  ·  Full Review

Longitudinal Outcome Evaluation

Cycles 3–4 completed  ·  Annual clinical review
Forward plan established  ·  Protocol refinement or continuation

The 12-month horizon review is a formal clinical evaluation conducted against the documented baseline established at the initial consultation. It is not a routine follow-up — it is a structured outcomes assessment, comparing every quantifiable metric against the pre-treatment record to evaluate the true therapeutic yield of the treatment program.

Headache frequency at Month 12 compared against pre-treatment baseline; responder status documented
Functional capacity assessment: occupational impact, sleep quality, quality-of-life metrics
Total cumulative dosage reviewed; safety and tolerability across four cycles documented
CGRP pathway efficacy independently evaluated; agent continued, substituted, or discontinued
Forward 12-month care architecture established based on full clinical evidence record
Cumulative Dose Across 12-Month Horizon (4 Cycles  ·  Estimated Range)
620–780u OnabotulinumtoxinA

Clinical protocols are individualized at Monti Institute. The dosage ranges, cycle structure, and outcome benchmarks illustrated above represent the evidence-based PREEMPT framework as a reference. No therapeutic plan is prescribed or implied by this visualization. All interventional decisions are made by Dr. Monti following formal clinical evaluation.

Methodology

Aesthetic Approach

01

Conservative, Buildable Results

Every treatment is staged incrementally and calibrated to tissue response — preserving natural movement and avoiding the cumulative distortion that accompanies overtreatment.

02

Anatomically Guided Planning

Treatment selection follows facial osteology, adipose compartment dynamics, and SMAS integrity — not aesthetic trends or patient volume requests.

03

Facial Balance Over Volume

We address the face as an integrated anatomical structure. Proportional integrity, light reflection, and three-dimensional balance take precedence over isolated volume correction.

04

Long-Term Aesthetic Evolution

Aesthetic care must account for the long arc of facial aging — including bony resorption, ligamentous laxity, and volumetric redistribution. Each intervention is designed with that trajectory in mind.

Clinical Protocols

Aesthetic Protocols

01

Full-Face Rebalancing

A comprehensive injectable assessment addressing volumetric loss, midface descent, and facial unit imbalance — restoring structural coherence across all anatomical zones.

02

Lip Refinement

Hyaluronic acid lip refinement guided by Cupid's bow architecture, philtral column definition, and vermilion proportion — never at the expense of natural movement or facial harmony.

03

Jawline & Chin Contouring

Injectable contouring of the mandibular border and chin projection — restoring structural definition without compromising the anatomical character of the face.

04

Skin Tightening & Resurfacing

Fractional laser and radiofrequency modalities targeting the dermal matrix — stimulating neocollagenesis and improving surface texture, tone, and structural tightening at the tissue level.

05

Collagen-Stimulating Therapies

Poly-L-lactic acid (Sculptra) and complementary biostimulatory agents — delivered to restore the collagenous scaffold and address volume loss driven by dermal matrix degradation and bony resorption.

06

Pigment & Vascular Correction

Intense Pulsed Light, Picosecond, and Nd:YAG laser modalities — targeting superficial and deeper chromophores for precise correction of pigmentation irregularity and vascular disruption.

Monti Institute  ·  Reno, Nevada

About
the Institute

At Monti Institute, neurological medicine and aesthetic care are practiced together within a single physician-led practice — built on a simple conviction: that how you feel and how you carry yourself are rarely separate concerns.

Why We Exist

A different kind of practice

There are excellent neurologists. There are excellent aesthetic providers. What is harder to find is a physician who understands both — and who has built a practice around that dual expertise with genuine depth in each.

Monti Institute was founded for patients who want more than a rushed appointment and a standard answer. For those managing migraine or chronic neurological symptoms, that means care that keeps pace with the real complexity of their condition. For those seeking aesthetic care, it means treatment guided by anatomy and clinical restraint rather than trend and volume.

The result is a practice that feels different — not because it is trying to, but because it is structured entirely differently.

Our Philosophy

Precision over volume

We made a deliberate decision not to scale. The practice is intentionally small, with a patient panel that reflects genuine clinical capacity rather than growth ambition.

This means longer appointments. More considered follow-up. A clinical team that knows you by your second visit, not your fifth. And a physician with enough continuity on your case to make genuinely good decisions — not just competent ones.

In most medical settings, volume is a business requirement. Here, restraint is.

Two Disciplines

Neurology and aesthetics, seen together

Most practices treat neurological care and aesthetic medicine as entirely separate domains. In our experience, they are not.

How patients experience their energy, their pain, their confidence, and their sense of themselves — these things are deeply connected. A patient managing chronic migraine carries burdens that extend well beyond headache frequency: disrupted sleep, lost workdays, social withdrawal, a quiet erosion of the life they want to be living. A patient seeking aesthetic refinement often has a considered reason — something meaningful to them about how they want to feel and present themselves.

We take both seriously. Every consultation — neurological or aesthetic — begins with the same question: what matters most to you right now, and what would genuinely improve your quality of life?

Patient Experience

What it feels like to be a patient here

We designed this practice around a simple idea: that a medical appointment should feel like an unhurried conversation with a physician who is genuinely paying attention.

Your first visit is not a triage. It is an extended consultation — time to discuss your full history, previous treatments, current symptoms, and what has and has not worked. From that foundation, we build a plan.

Follow-up is equally considered. We review what has changed, what hasn’t, and what requires adjustment. The goal is not a good outcome at one visit — it is a care relationship that improves over time, with a physician who knows your case.

Location

Reno, Nevada

Monti Institute is located at 2440 Vassar Street, Suite 3, in Reno, Nevada — a purpose-designed clinical environment that reflects the care and attention we bring to everything we do.

We serve patients from Reno, the broader Northern Nevada region, and the Western United States. For those traveling for specialist neurological or aesthetic care, we are pleased to assist with scheduling considerations that make the visit as straightforward as possible.

Hours & Access

Getting started

New patient consultations are scheduled by appointment. Our team reviews every inquiry and responds within one business day.

Insurance is accepted for neurological services. Aesthetic care is private-pay. Insurance verification is available on request prior to your first visit.

Dr. Ryan Monti is the founder and medical director of Monti Institute of Neuro Aesthetics — a physician whose clinical identity is defined by two things that rarely coexist in a single practice: academic-level expertise in neurological medicine and a deeply refined approach to aesthetic care.

He founded the Institute on a conviction born directly from clinical experience: that patients with chronic migraine and complex neurological conditions deserve more than an abbreviated appointment and a formulaic response. That patients seeking aesthetic refinement deserve more than volume-driven technique and trend-chasing outcomes. And that the physician who treats both is uniquely positioned to understand how profoundly they are connected.

Clinical Philosophy

Dr. Monti practices with a discipline that is increasingly rare in modern medicine: the discipline of restraint. In neurology, this means refusing to maintain a patient on a regimen that has stopped working — and committing to the longitudinal recalibration that meaningful neurological outcomes require. In aesthetics, it means treating the face as an integrated anatomical architecture, not a collection of features to be individually corrected. In both disciplines, it means knowing when not to intervene — and having the clinical confidence to say so.

Every treatment decision made at Monti Institute carries Dr. Monti’s direct clinical reasoning. He does not operate a practice that scales by delegating its most consequential decisions. Evaluations are unhurried. Diagnoses are precise. Plans are built from your anatomy, your history, and your goals — not assembled from a standard pathway.

Training & Academic Affiliation

Dr. Monti holds board certification in Internal Medicine and maintains active membership in the American College of Physicians (ACP) and the National Board of Physicians and Surgeons (NBPAS). He is a Fellow of the American Academy of Cannabis Medicine (FAACM®) and holds an academic appointment as Associate Professor at the Medical College of Georgia (MCG) — a relationship that keeps his clinical practice aligned with the standards and advances of academic medicine.

His subspecialty focus in migraine medicine and medical aesthetics reflects a deliberate, years-long commitment to clinical depth in both disciplines — not a broad generalist practice rebranded for market appeal.

Why He Built This Practice

The patients who come to Monti Institute are, with remarkable consistency, those who have been through the system and found it insufficient. They have seen the neurologist with the 12-minute appointment. They have tried the aesthetician who administered without evaluating. They are intelligent, discerning people who know the difference between care that is adequate and care that is genuinely excellent.

Dr. Monti built this practice for them. Not to be the largest neurological clinic in Northern Nevada, but to be the one where a physician with uncommon expertise takes the time to actually understand what a patient needs — and delivers it with the precision, continuity, and clinical seriousness it deserves.

Scholarly Activity

Select Research & Global Presentations

What follows is not a formality. These contributions represent a decade of active clinical inquiry into the most demanding territories of internal and neurovascular medicine — the same depth of understanding that informs every diagnostic and interventional decision made at this practice today.

Vascular Pharmacotherapy  ·  Published Research

Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors, Endothelin Antagonists & Prostacyclin Analogs in the Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism

WASET International Conference on Internal Medicine  ·  Published & Presented, 2016

An investigation into the pharmacological management of acute pulmonary embolism using three distinct classes of vasodilatory agents: phosphodiesterase inhibitors, endothelin receptor antagonists, and prostacyclin analogs. The research examined the hemodynamic rationale for each class, their respective mechanisms of action on pulmonary vascular resistance, and their clinical application in acute, life-threatening presentations.

Selected for publication and international presentation at the World Academy of Science, Engineering and Technology (WASET) International Conference on Internal Medicine — peer-reviewed and presented to an international medical audience.

Clinical relevance:  A physician who has published on acute pulmonary vascular pharmacotherapy has an intimate understanding of systemic circulatory physiology, hemodynamic instability, and the vascular consequences of intervention. That depth directly informs the precision and systemic safety standards applied in neuro-aesthetic and interventional neurology practice.
Advanced Cardiology  ·  International Poster · Berlin

Left Ventricular Pseudo-Aneurysm Following Undocumented Myocardial Infarction

8th Global Cardiology Conference  ·  Berlin, Germany  ·  2016

A case report documenting a rare and diagnostically elusive complication: left ventricular pseudo-aneurysm formation in a patient with no known cardiac history and no prior cardiac surgery. The case required a precise synthesis of clinical pattern recognition, cardiac imaging interpretation, and an understanding of post-infarct structural sequelae that are missed when the inciting event is never documented.

Clinical relevance:  Mastery of cardiovascular structural pathology and the ability to reason from incomplete clinical histories are directly transferable to complex neurological and aesthetic patient evaluation — where undocumented histories and atypical presentations are the rule, not the exception.
Neurovascular Medicine  ·  Featured Case · Human Dx

Temporal Lobe Hemorrhagic Stroke Presenting as Déjà Vu

Global Morning Report  ·  Human Dx Project  ·  2016

A diagnostically exceptional case in which a temporal lobe hemorrhagic stroke presented not with the hallmark signs of acute neurological event — sudden weakness, facial droop, loss of speech — but with the subtle and easily dismissed symptom of déjà vu. Selected for the Human Dx Global Morning Report, a curated platform on which the world’s most challenging and instructive cases are surfaced for the global physician community.

Clinical relevance:  In migraine and headache medicine, the ability to distinguish a benign neurological symptom from a harbinger of intracranial pathology is not a textbook exercise — it is the defining clinical skill. This case demonstrates exactly the level of neurovascular pattern recognition that underpins the diagnostic safety of this practice.
Gastroenterology  ·  National Poster · ACG 2017

Radiation-Induced Aorto-Esophageal Fistula: How Recognizing the Chiari Triad Enables Life-Saving Early Intervention

American College of Gastroenterology Annual Scientific Meeting  ·  ACG 2017  ·  National Poster Presentation

A case study in critical clinical pattern recognition: the identification of a radiation-induced aorto-esophageal fistula — a rare and near-uniformly fatal complication — through early recognition of the Chiari Triad (mid-thoracic pain, sentinel arterial hemorrhage, and delayed exsanguination). The presentation argued that this triad, when recognized early, creates a narrow window for life-saving surgical intervention that does not exist once the full complication unfolds.

Clinical relevance:  The clinical discipline of recognizing rare but catastrophic patterns before they become irreversible — and acting within the window of opportunity — is precisely the quality that defines both the safety standard and the diagnostic culture of this practice.

Legal & Compliance

Privacy Policy

Effective Date: January 1, 2025  ·  HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices  ·  Monti Institute of Neuro Aesthetics, LLC

1. Overview & Scope

Monti Institute of Neuro Aesthetics, LLC (“Monti Institute,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) is committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal information and your Protected Health Information (“PHI”) as required under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (“HIPAA”) and its implementing regulations, including the HITECH Act amendments.

This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard personal and health information gathered through our website (monti-institute.com), online booking system, patient intake forms, patient portal, and related communications. This document also serves as our HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices.

2. Information We Collect

Personal Identification Information: Name, date of birth, email address, telephone number, and mailing address — collected through contact forms, booking requests, and patient intake.

Protected Health Information (PHI): Medical history, health conditions, treatment preferences, clinical notes, and other health-related data submitted through our patient intake process, in-person clinical consultations, or via the Boulevard patient portal.

Payment Information: Credit or debit card information collected and processed securely through our practice management and payment processor. Monti Institute does not store full card numbers on our own systems.

Technical & Usage Data: IP address, browser type, operating system, pages visited, time spent on site, and referring URL — collected automatically through standard web analytics tools.

Cookie Data: Please see Section 8 (Cookie Policy) for full disclosure.

3. How We Use Your Information

We use your personal and health information solely for the following permitted purposes:

  • To schedule, coordinate, and deliver clinical services and treatments;
  • To communicate appointment confirmations, reminders, and follow-up care information;
  • To process payments and manage your account;
  • To fulfill supplement orders placed through our Fullscript practitioner dispensary;
  • To comply with applicable federal and state laws and regulatory requirements;
  • To operate, improve, and secure our website and digital services;
  • To send operational communications you have consented to receive.

We do not sell, rent, or lease your personal or health information to any third party for marketing purposes, under any circumstances.

4. Disclosure of Your Information — Trusted Third Parties

We may share your information only as permitted or required by HIPAA and applicable law, including with the following compliant service providers with whom Monti Institute maintains executed Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) where required:

  • Boulevard (blvd.app): Our HIPAA-aligned practice management, scheduling, and patient portal platform. Appointment data, intake information, and communications are transmitted and stored through Boulevard’s encrypted infrastructure.
  • Fullscript: Our compliant practitioner supplement dispensary. Name and email may be transmitted when we provision a patient account for supplement protocol access.
  • Payment Processor: Credit card and payment data is processed through PCI-DSS compliant payment infrastructure integrated with Boulevard.
  • Legal and Regulatory Authorities: We may disclose information as required by court order, subpoena, or applicable law, including to state medical licensing boards.

5. Your HIPAA Rights

As a patient of Monti Institute, you have the following rights with respect to your PHI:

  • Right to Access: Request a copy of your PHI maintained in our records;
  • Right to Amend: Request corrections to inaccurate or incomplete PHI;
  • Right to an Accounting of Disclosures: Request a list of certain disclosures of your PHI;
  • Right to Request Restrictions: Request limits on how we use or disclose your PHI;
  • Right to Confidential Communications: Request that we communicate with you by alternative means or at an alternate location;
  • Right to File a Complaint: File a complaint with us or with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights if you believe your privacy rights have been violated. We will not retaliate against you for filing a complaint.

To exercise any of these rights, contact our Privacy Officer at admin@monti-institute.com.

6. Data Security

Monti Institute implements administrative, physical, and technical safeguards reasonably designed to protect your PHI and personal information against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. These measures include:

  • End-to-end encryption of patient data transmitted through Boulevard;
  • Access controls limiting PHI access to authorized clinical personnel only;
  • Secure, credential-protected patient portal login;
  • Periodic risk assessments consistent with HIPAA Security Rule requirements.

No data transmission over the internet or electronic storage system is 100% secure. While we take commercially reasonable precautions, we cannot guarantee absolute security.

7. Data Retention

We retain patient medical records in accordance with Nevada Revised Statutes governing healthcare record retention (generally seven (7) years for adult patient records from the date of last service, or longer as required). Non-clinical personal data is retained only as long as necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, or as required by applicable law.

8. Cookie Policy & Tracking Transparency

Our website may use the following types of cookies and tracking technologies:

  • Essential Cookies: Required for core site functionality including navigation, session management, and security. These cannot be disabled without impairing site function.
  • Analytics Cookies: Aggregate, anonymized data on how visitors use our Site (e.g., pages visited, time on site). This data does not identify individual users and is used solely to improve site performance.
  • Third-Party Embed Cookies: Our booking widget (Boulevard) may set session cookies required for the booking overlay to function properly.

We do not use advertising, behavioral, or cross-site tracking cookies. You may configure your browser to refuse certain cookies, though this may affect site functionality.

9. Children’s Privacy

Our Site and services are not directed to individuals under the age of 18. We do not knowingly collect personal information from minors. If we become aware that a minor has provided personal information without verified parental consent, we will take steps to delete such information promptly.

10. Contact — Privacy Officer

For privacy inquiries, PHI access requests, or to report a suspected privacy breach:

Scheduling & Financial Policy

Booking, Cancellation & Refund Policy

Effective Date: January 1, 2025  ·  Monti Institute of Neuro Aesthetics, LLC  ·  Reno, Nevada

1. Appointment Booking & Confirmation

All appointments at Monti Institute of Neuro Aesthetics are scheduled through our authorized online booking system (Boulevard) or directly via our Clinical Operations Team. An appointment is considered confirmed only upon receipt of a written or digital confirmation from Monti Institute and, where applicable, receipt of any required deposit.

New patient consultations are scheduled following the completion of our structured pre-assessment intake process. Submitting a booking request does not guarantee an appointment slot until confirmation is issued.

2. Credit Card on File — Authorization

A valid credit or debit card on file is required for all scheduled appointments. By booking with Monti Institute, you expressly authorize us to charge the card on file for any applicable late-cancellation fees, no-show fees, and any outstanding balances for services rendered, subject to the terms set forth in this Policy. Your card will not be charged for a routine appointment unless a fee is triggered under Sections 3 or 4 below.

Card information is stored securely through our PCI-DSS compliant payment processor and is never retained on our own servers in unencrypted form. You may update your card on file through the patient portal or by contacting our office directly.

3. Cancellation Policy — 48-Hour Notice Required

All appointment cancellations and reschedule requests must be received by Monti Institute at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to your scheduled appointment time. Cancellations within this window must be communicated directly to our office by telephone or email at admin@monti-institute.com.

Late Cancellation Fee: Cancellations received less than 48 hours before the scheduled appointment time will result in a late-cancellation fee charged to the card on file. The fee schedule is as follows:

  • Cancellation with 24–48 hours notice: $[XX] or [XX]% of the scheduled service value — confirm with your clinic
  • Cancellation with less than 24 hours notice: $[XX] or [XX]% of the scheduled service value

Fees are applied at our discretion and may be waived in documented cases of medical emergency.

4. No-Show Policy

No-Show Fee: Failure to appear for a scheduled appointment without prior notice constitutes a no-show. A no-show fee of $[XX] or [XX]% of the scheduled service value (up to the full service charge) will be charged to the card on file. Repeat no-shows may result in a requirement for prepayment of future appointments or termination of the clinical relationship at our discretion.

5. Deposits & Prepayment

Certain appointment types, including complex multi-service appointments, new patient consultations, or bookings following a prior no-show, may require a non-refundable deposit at the time of booking. Deposit amounts will be disclosed at the time of scheduling. Deposits are applied to the balance of the scheduled service if the appointment is honored.

6. Service Refund Policy — No Refunds on Rendered Services

All clinical services, treatments, and professional fees are non-refundable once rendered. This applies to:

  • Initial and follow-up clinical consultations;
  • Neuromodulator (Botox/Dysport) treatments and injectable services;
  • Dermal filler and structural aesthetic procedures;
  • Advanced regenerative and energy-based treatments;
  • Any additional clinical service performed during your appointment.

If you are dissatisfied with a clinical outcome, you are encouraged to contact our office promptly. We are committed to addressing clinical concerns through appropriate follow-up evaluation. Dissatisfaction with a result does not constitute grounds for a refund of fees for services rendered.

7. Supplement Refund Policy

Medical-grade supplements ordered through our Fullscript practitioner dispensary are non-refundable once the order has been placed and fulfilled. Supplement protocols are customized clinical recommendations and cannot be restocked or resold. If you receive a defective or incorrect product, please contact Fullscript directly through the dispensary platform for resolution.

8. Clinical Credit & Gift Credit Policy

Clinical credits (including gift credits purchased for another person) are non-refundable and non-transferable to cash. Clinical credits carry no expiration date and may be applied to any service or product offered by Monti Institute. Credits are transferable to another named individual only with prior written authorization from our office.

9. Package & Prepaid Protocol Policy

Prepaid treatment packages and longitudinal care protocols are non-refundable once initiated. If you choose to discontinue a prepaid protocol prior to completion, any unused credits may be retained on account for future services at our discretion. No cash refunds will be issued for partially completed packages.

10. Contact — Scheduling & Financial Inquiries

For questions regarding this policy, to update your card on file, or to communicate a cancellation:
Clinical Operations Team — Monti Institute
admin@monti-institute.com  ·  (321) DR-MONTI

Accessibility & Inclusion

Digital Accessibility Statement

Effective Date: January 1, 2025  ·  Monti Institute of Neuro Aesthetics, LLC  ·  WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance

1. Our Commitment

Monti Institute of Neuro Aesthetics, LLC is committed to ensuring that our website and all digital services are accessible to individuals with disabilities, including those who rely on screen readers, keyboard navigation, voice control, magnification software, or other assistive technologies.

We believe that every patient—regardless of physical or cognitive ability—deserves equitable access to our clinical information, booking systems, and patient portal. Digital accessibility is not an accommodation. It is a standard of care.

2. Conformance Status — WCAG 2.1 Level AA

Monti Institute actively works toward conformance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Level AA, as published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). These guidelines define requirements for improving web accessibility across four principles:

  • Perceivable: Information and interface components must be presentable in ways users can perceive. We maintain high-contrast text ratios (minimum 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text), provide meaningful alt text for all informative images, and do not use color alone to convey meaning.
  • Operable: All interface components and navigation are fully keyboard accessible. We provide visible focus indicators, skip navigation links, and avoid content that flashes more than three times per second.
  • Understandable: The page language is declared in HTML, forms include explicit label associations, and error messages are descriptively communicated.
  • Robust: Our Site is built with semantic HTML5 landmark roles, ARIA attributes where appropriate, and is tested for compatibility with leading screen reader and assistive technology combinations.

Our website is currently in active pre-launch development. Accessibility testing and remediation is ongoing. We acknowledge that some areas may not yet fully conform to WCAG 2.1 AA and are committed to continuous improvement.

3. Known Limitations

While we strive for full conformance, the following known areas are actively under review:

  • Third-party booking overlay (Boulevard) and supplement dispensary (Fullscript): Accessibility of these embedded platforms is governed by the respective vendors. We have communicated our accessibility standards to these partners and encourage users to report any barriers encountered within these embedded systems.
  • Complex clinical diagrams or anatomical illustrations may include extended descriptions upon request.
  • PDF documents or downloadable forms may require remediation for screen reader compatibility.

4. Report an Accessibility Barrier

If you encounter any barrier to accessibility on our website or digital platforms, we ask that you contact us directly so that we may provide the information or assistance you need and remediate the issue. We are committed to responding to all accessibility reports within two (2) business days.

Accessibility Contact — Monti Institute Administration
Email: admin@monti-institute.com
Phone: (321) DR-MONTI
Subject Line: Digital Accessibility Report
Office Hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (Pacific Time)

Please describe the specific barrier you encountered, the page or feature affected, and the assistive technology or browser you were using. We will respond with either a direct solution or a manual alternative accommodation.

5. External Complaint Pathways

If you are unsatisfied with our response to an accessibility report, you may contact the following regulatory bodies:

  • U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division — Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA): ada.gov
  • Section 508 Coordinator (applicable federal standards): section508.gov

6. Ongoing Assessment

Monti Institute conducts periodic accessibility evaluations using a combination of automated testing tools and manual review. Our development team references the W3C’s WCAG 2.1 criteria and evaluates our Site against assistive technology combinations including NVDA + Firefox, JAWS + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari, and TalkBack on Android.

This Accessibility Statement was last reviewed and updated on January 1, 2025. We will review and update this statement as improvements are made to our digital platforms.
